newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ARS charges don't help gem talks -De Beers source.
newsitem.headline: ARS charges don't help gem talks -De Beers source.

text.p: A De Beers official said on Tuesday that an investigation by Russia's prosecutor general into the finances of Russian diamond firm Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS) could affect talks on a major export deal.
"Clearly, if that (the charges) is true, it can't be helpful," Raymond Clarke, head of De Beers' Moscow representation, told Reuters, when asked how the talks would be affected.
He declined to be more specific, saying only that De Beers had not discussed the issue with ARS but that it would seek clarification from ARS officials.

He also declined to say when an agreement to export Russian diamonds -- the text of which Russian government and ministry officials are in the process of examining before approving -- could be signed.

Interfax news agency said the prosecutor general's office had launched an investigation into ARS over alleged currency violations and tax evasion, saying that fines for hard currency violations alone could total $379 million.

ARS, which is Russia's largest diamond producer and sole authorised exporter and accounts for one quarter of world diamond output, is De Beers' negotiating partner in a crucial deal to export diamonds that is awaiting government approval.
ARS officials were unavailable for comment.
ARS is largely responsible for steering the agreement through the Russian government and various ministries.
Russian officials have launched a major crackdown in recent weeks on profitable and unprofitable enterprises to boost budget revenues and overcome tax shortfalls.
De Beers and ARS last month produced a framework agreement based on a February memorandum for a three-year export deal and are awaiting government officials' signatures.
ARS awarded NatWest Markets a mandate in July to raise $500 million in funding over two years to finance exploration and mining.
